title: We replaced Redis with MySQL for inventory reservations—and it scaled (2026) - Shopify
excerpt: How we used SKIP LOCKED, composite primary keys, and connection visibility to hit our scale targets.
content_html:
During checkout, when a buyer clicks "Complete purchase," we need to guarantee the items they're buying are still available. If we get this wrong in one direction, two buyers purchase the same last unit: the merchant has to cancel an order, send an apology email, and eat the support cost. If we get it wrong in the other direction, we tell a buyer something is sold out when it isn't, and the merchant loses a sale they should have made.

At Shopify's scale, either failure compounds fast. On Black Friday 2025, merchants on our platform hit a record $5.1 million in sales per minute at peak. Every one of those transactions touches inventory.

Our oversell protection system handles this by reserving inventory during payment processing—a short hold that prevents two concurrent checkouts from claiming the same unit. For years, this ran on Redis. When we moved toward a unified database strategy, we had to answer a hard question: could MySQL handle the same scale?

Earlier attempts had failed. A single row with a quantity column couldn't handle the contention. MySQL 8's SKIP LOCKED feature introduced a different design: one row per inventory unit instead of one row per item. Inspired by 37signals' approach to database-backed load distribution, we rebuilt reservations on MySQL and hit our high-throughput targets during peak 2025 traffic.

But the hardest lesson wasn't about database design. It was discovering that the real bottleneck wasn’t what we were observing and measuring. This post walks through the solution and what we found along the way.

The challenge

What is oversell protection?

Oversell protection has two main operations:

  • Reserve: When payment starts, we mark items as reserved (a short hold, e.g. several minutes).
  • Claim: When payment succeeds, we permanently deduct quantity from the inventory ledger (source of truth).

Checkout completion depends on this being fast and correct. Slow reservations trigger throttling and a worse buyer experience. Mistakes mean overselling (angry customers) or underselling (lost revenue).

Scale and correctness requirements

Scale here is not abstract: Shopify powers over 14% of U.S. ecommerce, and on Black Friday 2025 we saw an 11% increase in sales per minute at peak over the prior year. Reservations run on every checkout that touches inventory, so the system must handle that burst without dropping requests or breaking consistency.

We needed to:

  • Support the platform's high-performance throughput targets during peak traffic
  • Respect multi-location inventory (only reserve from locations that can fulfill)
  • Keep ACID guarantees between reservations and the inventory ledger
  • Prioritize correctness: no overselling and no lost reservations

The Redis model and its limits

The previous system stored reservations in Redis. Each item had a quantity key, and reserving meant DECR, releasing meant INCR. Redis handled concurrency fine, but reservations and the inventory ledger lived in two different systems.

The claim step (payment processed, permanently deduct inventory) required updating MySQL and cleaning up Redis, and those two operations couldn't be wrapped in a single atomic step. Depending on the order, this could cause overselling (item sold but was never deducted from the ledger) or underselling (item deducted and still marked reserved).

On top of that, the Redis model had no multi-location awareness and added the operational cost of a separate cluster to maintain. Moving reservations into the same MySQL database as the ledger meant we could wrap everything in ACID transactions and eliminate these failure modes entirely.

The solution: SKIP LOCKED

Core idea: one row per unit, bounded by design

Instead of one row per item with a quantity column, we use one row per sellable unit. An item with 10 units has 10 rows. Reserving three units means selecting and moving three rows in a single transaction. By keeping reservations and the inventory ledger in the same database, we get ACID across reserve and claim—fixing classes of bugs that were possible with Redis (e.g. payment succeeds but inventory isn't claimed, or the reverse).

SKIP LOCKED is what makes this scalable: if another transaction has locked some rows, MySQL skips them and returns other available rows. No waiting on the same row, less contention.

But one row per unit for all inventory would break down at scale—an item with 50,000 units across 10 locations would mean 500,000 rows, and the reserve query would slow as it scans through them. Instead, we maintain a bounded pool of available rows, capped at 1,000 per item/location combination. Reservations consume rows from this pool; a replenishment process refills it from the inventory ledger.

Why 1,000? The cap needs to be large enough to absorb bursts without running dry, but small enough to keep the table compact and the SKIP LOCKED scan fast. We sized it based on observed peak reservation rates per item/location during flash sales: 1,000 gives us enough headroom that replenishment can keep up under sustained load without the table growing to a point where query performance degrades.

What happens if the pool empties? During an extreme flash sale, the pool for a hot item can be temporarily exhausted. When that happens, the reserve path triggers replenishment inline. A lock ensures only one transaction replenishes at a time; other concurrent reserves for the same item wait for it to finish rather than all racing to insert rows, avoiding a thundering herd. Once replenishment completes, the waiting transactions proceed with a full pool. The buyer never sees the item as unavailable (unless it truly is). This adds latency to that specific reservation, but it preserves correctness: a buyer with available inventory is never turned away.

Key technical decisions

1. Composite primary key: fewer locks per row

Our first prototype used an auto-increment ID as the primary key. When we observed lock behavior (e.g. with SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS), we saw two row locks per reservation instead of one.

With an auto-increment primary key, InnoDB was locking both the secondary index used in the WHERE clause and the clustered index (primary key). We switched to a composite primary key (shop_id, inventory_item_id, inventory_group_id, id) so the columns we filter on are part of the primary key. That reduced to one lock per row, which was important when running many reservations per second.

Takeaway: at this scale, index and primary key design directly affect lock count and throughput.

2. READ COMMITTED: avoiding gap (supremum) locks

When we ran SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on an empty table that needed replenishment, we saw gap locks (including on the "supremum" pseudo-record). Those locks blocked the replenishment transaction from inserting new rows and could lead to deadlocks.

We changed the transaction isolation level from REPEATABLE READ (MySQL default) to READ COMMITTED for these transactions. Under READ COMMITTED, InnoDB doesn't take gap locks in the same way, so replenishment could proceed. Jahfer Husain's guide to InnoDB locking was very helpful for understanding this. This was our first use of a non-default isolation level in this codebase; it required small framework support for setting isolation per transaction.

3. Consistent lock ordering: avoiding deadlocks

We hit deadlocks when reserve and claim touched two tables in different orders. Reserve was doing INSERT into reserved_quantities then DELETE from reservation_units; claim was doing DELETE from reserved_quantities. Different transactions could lock the two tables in different orders and form a cycle.

The fix was to standardize the order: reserve always DELETEs from the units table first, then INSERTs into reserved_quantities. Claim only touches reserved_quantities. Because both paths now acquire locks in the same order, neither can hold a lock the other is waiting for—no more circular waits.

4. Batching with UNION ALL

Each round trip to the database has a cost. For carts with multiple line items, we batch reservation queries using UNION ALL so we fetch all needed units in one round trip:

That cut total round trips and helped latency under load.

The real bottleneck: connections, not CPU

In production we hit a throughput ceiling well below our target. Reservation latency (e.g. P90) was acceptable, CPU wasn't maxed out, and the queries were already optimized. So we looked elsewhere.

We tried batching reservations across multiple checkouts in a single SKIP LOCKED query to use fewer connections. That helped in load tests but added complexity. We also moved some read load to replicas. Still, something didn't add up.

Following the symptoms

During load tests we saw:

  • Threads queuing in MySQL
  • CPU spiking when queued work ran
  • Connection exhaustion to MySQL backends on ProxySQL layer

So we added visibility into which business processes were holding database connections and for how long. Knowing that connections are exhausted doesn't tell you who is holding them. We needed per-caller attribution.

On the application side, we annotated every SQL statement with a comment tag identifying the business process, like /* conn_tag:checkout_completion */. On the ProxySQL layer, we added tracking that parses the tag and measures how long each caller holds a connection. The result: total connection hold time, broken down by business process.

This immediately showed which callers were consuming the most connection time. Not which queries were slow, but which processes were holding connections across long transactions. If you're hitting connection limits and can't tell why, this pattern (tag at the app layer, aggregate at the proxy) is straightforward to implement and immediately actionable.

What we found

Once we could see connection usage, we learned that reservations weren't the only heavy user. Other parts of the checkout path were holding connections longer than necessary. They hadn't been optimized because they hadn't been the first to hit the limit. Connections are finite: at high throughput we need many short transactions per second. When other code held connections longer, reservations were the straw that broke the camel's back—not because reservations were slow, but because the pool was already near depletion.

The cleanup of the checkout path removed 50% of reads and 33% of transactions on the primary database. We also revisited MySQL configuration. InnoDB thread concurrency had been set conservatively years earlier and never re-evaluated. Our workload had changed. After increasing thread concurrency where we had headroom, we removed a bottleneck we hadn't seen until we had connection and CPU metrics side by side.

Combined, the cleanup and configuration changes removed the ceiling. We could scale beyond our previous limit and meet our targets. During high-volume flash sales, writer CPU stayed under 50% and reader CPU under 16%, with headroom to spare.

The cutover

We didn't flip a switch from Redis to MySQL. We ran both systems in parallel in what we called "shadow mode": every reservation was written to both Redis and MySQL, with Redis remaining the source of truth. This let us compare the two systems side by side, validating that MySQL produced the correct business outcomes and met our performance requirements on real production traffic. Because both systems were live, there were no in-flight reservations to migrate. Redis reservations continued to be honored while MySQL built up its own state.

Once we were satisfied with correctness and performance, we switched the source of truth to MySQL. If anything went wrong, we could revert to Redis with a kill switch; the dual-write path was still active, so Redis had a complete view of reservations at all times. The rollout was gradual, pod by pod, starting with low-traffic pods and working up to our highest-volume merchants.

What we learned

We learned so much from this project but the two main takeaways:

1. Revisit old decisions

What wasn't possible five years ago (e.g. MySQL for this workload) can be possible today with new features like SKIP LOCKED. The same goes for configuration: thread limits and other "rule of thumb" settings are worth re-checking when workload and hardware evolve. If the numbers don't add up (e.g. low CPU but queuing), dig in.

2. Start small and observe

We got a lot of value from a minimal prototype: a small ruby script and MySQL, no full framework like Rails. Observing the database (e.g. lock behavior in a second terminal) taught us more than theory alone. Simple tooling and a tight feedback loop beat big, opaque systems when exploring.

MySQL can now handle workloads we used to assume required specialized infrastructure. If you're reaching for Redis, Kafka, or a custom coordination layer for high-throughput mutual exclusion, your existing database might already be enough.

The bottleneck wasn't where we expected. We optimized queries and locks for weeks; the real limit was connection usage in code we weren't even looking at. If the numbers don't add up—low CPU but high queuing—instrument the full path. The answer is often in the plumbing, not the engine.

Crucially, this wasn't about making reservations fast. It was about making them safe neighbors. Reservations share a database with cart updates, payment processing, and order creation. A system that saturates connections or holds locks too long jeopardizes all of them. The real bar was sustaining throughput without degrading database health for everything else.

For us, the payoff is concrete: more reliable reservations mean no oversells and more successful purchases from our merchants.

sentences.en: Mistakes mean overselling (angry customers) or underselling (lost revenue).

blocks.html_en: Scale and correctness requirements

sentences.en: Scale and correctness requirements
sentences.zh: 规模和正确性要求

blocks.html_en: Scale here is not abstract: Shopify powers over 14% of U.S. ecommerce, and on Black Friday 2025 we saw an 11% increase in sales per minute at peak over the prior year. Reservations run on every checkout that touches inventory, so the system must handle that burst without dropping requests or breaking consistency.

sentences.en: Scale here is not abstract: Shopify powers over 14% of U.S. ecommerce, and on Black Friday 2025 we saw an 11% increase in sales per minute at peak over the prior year.
sentences.zh: 这里的规模并不是抽象的：Shopify 占据了超过 14% 的美国电子商务市场，在 2025 年黑色星期五，我们看到每分钟的销售额比去年同期增长了 11%。

sentences.en: Reservations run on every checkout that touches inventory, so the system must handle that burst without dropping requests or breaking consistency.
sentences.zh: 每次涉及库存的结账都会进行预订，因此系统必须在不丢弃请求或破坏一致性的情况下处理突发情况。

blocks.html_en: We needed to:

sentences.en: We needed to:
sentences.zh: 我们需要：

blocks.html_en: • Support the platform's high-performance throughput targets during peak traffic

sentences.en: Support the platform's high-performance throughput targets during peak traffic
sentences.zh: 在高峰流量期间支持平台的高性能吞吐量目标

blocks.html_en: • Respect multi-location inventory (only reserve from locations that can fulfill)

sentences.en: Respect multi-location inventory (only reserve from locations that can fulfill)
sentences.zh: 尊重多地点库存（仅从可以履行的地点进行预订）

blocks.html_en: • Keep ACID guarantees between reservations and the inventory ledger

sentences.en: Keep ACID guarantees between reservations and the inventory ledger
sentences.zh: 在预订和库存分类账之间保持 ACID 保证

blocks.html_en: • Prioritize correctness: no overselling and no lost reservations

sentences.en: Prioritize correctness: no overselling and no lost reservations
sentences.zh: 优先考虑正确性：不超售，不丢失预订

blocks.html_en: The Redis model and its limits

sentences.en: The Redis model and its limits
sentences.zh: Redis 模型及其局限性

blocks.html_en: The previous system stored reservations in Redis. Each item had a quantity key, and reserving meant DECR, releasing meant INCR. Redis handled concurrency fine, but reservations and the inventory ledger lived in two different systems.

sentences.en: The previous system stored reservations in Redis.
sentences.zh: 以前的系统将预订存储在 Redis 中。

sentences.en: Each item had a quantity key, and reserving meant DECR, releasing meant INCR.
sentences.zh: 每个项目都有一个数量键，保留意味着 DECR，释放意味着 INCR。

sentences.en: Redis handled concurrency fine, but reservations and the inventory ledger lived in two different systems.
sentences.zh: Redis 可以很好地处理并发性，但预订和库存分类账位于两个不同的系统中。

blocks.html_en: The claim step (payment processed, permanently deduct inventory) required updating MySQL and cleaning up Redis, and those two operations couldn't be wrapped in a single atomic step. Depending on the order, this could cause overselling (item sold but was never deducted from the ledger) or underselling (item deducted and still marked reserved).

sentences.en: The claim step (payment processed, permanently deduct inventory) required updating MySQL and cleaning up Redis, and those two operations couldn't be wrapped in a single atomic step.
sentences.zh: 索赔步骤（处理付款、永久扣除库存）需要更新 MySQL 和清理 Redis，而这两个操作无法包含在单个原子步骤中。

sentences.en: Depending on the order, this could cause overselling (item sold but was never deducted from the ledger) or underselling (item deducted and still marked reserved).
sentences.zh: 根据订单，这可能会导致超售（商品已售出但从未从分类账中扣除）或卖空（商品已扣除但仍标记为保留）。

blocks.html_en: On top of that, the Redis model had no multi-location awareness and added the operational cost of a separate cluster to maintain. Moving reservations into the same MySQL database as the ledger meant we could wrap everything in ACID transactions and eliminate these failure modes entirely.

sentences.en: On top of that, the Redis model had no multi-location awareness and added the operational cost of a separate cluster to maintain.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，Redis 模型没有多位置意识，并且增加了维护单独集群的运营成本。

sentences.en: Moving reservations into the same MySQL database as the ledger meant we could wrap everything in ACID transactions and eliminate these failure modes entirely.
sentences.zh: 将预订转移到与账本相同的 MySQL 数据库中意味着我们可以将所有内容包装在 ACID 事务中，并完全消除这些故障模式。

blocks.html_en: The solution: SKIP LOCKED

sentences.en: The solution: SKIP LOCKED
sentences.zh: 解决方案：跳过锁定

blocks.html_en: Core idea: one row per unit, bounded by design

sentences.en: Core idea: one row per unit, bounded by design
sentences.zh: 核心理念：每单元一行，以设计为界

blocks.html_en: Instead of one row per item with a quantity column, we use one row per sellable unit. An item with 10 units has 10 rows. Reserving three units means selecting and moving three rows in a single transaction. By keeping reservations and the inventory ledger in the same database, we get ACID across reserve and claim—fixing classes of bugs that were possible with Redis (e.g. payment succeeds but inventory isn't claimed, or the reverse).

sentences.en: Instead of one row per item with a quantity column, we use one row per sellable unit.
sentences.zh: 我们使用每个可销售单位一行，而不是每个商品一行包含数量列。

sentences.en: An item with 10 units has 10 rows.
sentences.zh: 包含 10 个单位的项目有 10 行。

sentences.en: Reserving three units means selecting and moving three rows in a single transaction.
sentences.zh: 保留三个单元意味着在单个事务中选择并移动三行。

sentences.en: By keeping reservations and the inventory ledger in the same database, we get ACID across reserve and claim—fixing classes of bugs that were possible with Redis (e.g. payment succeeds but inventory isn't claimed, or the reverse).
sentences.zh: 通过将预订和库存分类账保存在同一个数据库中，我们可以在预订和索赔之间获得 ACID - 修复 Redis 可能出现的错误类别（例如，付款成功但库存未索赔，反之亦然）。

blocks.html_en: A simplified reserve flow looks like this:

sentences.en: A simplified reserve flow looks like this:
sentences.zh: 简化的储备流程如下所示：

blocks.html_en: SKIP LOCKED is what makes this scalable: if another transaction has locked some rows, MySQL skips them and returns other available rows. No waiting on the same row, less contention.

sentences.en: SKIP LOCKED is what makes this scalable: if another transaction has locked some rows, MySQL skips them and returns other available rows.
sentences.zh: SKIP LOCKED 使其具有可扩展性：如果另一个事务锁定了某些行，MySQL 会跳过它们并返回其他可用行。

sentences.en: No waiting on the same row, less contention.
sentences.zh: 无需在同一排等待，减少争用。

blocks.html_en: But one row per unit for all inventory would break down at scale—an item with 50,000 units across 10 locations would mean 500,000 rows, and the reserve query would slow as it scans through them. Instead, we maintain a bounded pool of available rows, capped at 1,000 per item/location combination. Reservations consume rows from this pool; a replenishment process refills it from the inventory ledger.

sentences.en: But one row per unit for all inventory would break down at scale—an item with 50,000 units across 10 locations would mean 500,000 rows, and the reserve query would slow as it scans through them.
sentences.zh: 但是，所有库存的每单位一行将出现大规模故障 - 跨 10 个位置的 50,000 单位的商品意味着 500,000 行，并且储备查询在扫描它们时会变慢。

sentences.en: Instead, we maintain a bounded pool of available rows, capped at 1,000 per item/location combination.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们维护一个有界的可用行池，每个项目/位置组合的上限为 1,000。

sentences.en: Reservations consume rows from this pool; a replenishment process refills it from the inventory ledger.
sentences.zh: 预留消耗该池中的行；补货流程会从库存分类账中重新填充它。

blocks.html_en: Why 1,000? The cap needs to be large enough to absorb bursts without running dry, but small enough to keep the table compact and the SKIP LOCKED scan fast. We sized it based on observed peak reservation rates per item/location during flash sales: 1,000 gives us enough headroom that replenishment can keep up under sustained load without the table growing to a point where query performance degrades.

sentences.zh: 为什么是 1,000？

sentences.en: The cap needs to be large enough to absorb bursts without running dry, but small enough to keep the table compact and the SKIP LOCKED scan fast.
sentences.zh: 上限需要足够大，以吸收突发而不至于耗尽，但又足够小，以保持表紧凑和 SKIP LOCKED 扫描快速。

sentences.en: We sized it based on observed peak reservation rates per item/location during flash sales: 1,000 gives us enough headroom that replenishment can keep up under sustained load without the table growing to a point where query performance degrades.
sentences.zh: 我们根据在闪购期间观察到的每个商品/位置的峰值预订率来确定其大小：1,000 为我们提供了足够的空间，可以在持续负载下保持补货，而不会导致表增长到查询性能下降的程度。

blocks.html_en: What happens if the pool empties? During an extreme flash sale, the pool for a hot item can be temporarily exhausted. When that happens, the reserve path triggers replenishment inline. A lock ensures only one transaction replenishes at a time; other concurrent reserves for the same item wait for it to finish rather than all racing to insert rows, avoiding a thundering herd. Once replenishment completes, the waiting transactions proceed with a full pool. The buyer never sees the item as unavailable (unless it truly is). This adds latency to that specific reservation, but it preserves correctness: a buyer with available inventory is never turned away.

sentences.en: What happens if the pool empties?
sentences.zh: 如果池空了会发生什么？

sentences.en: During an extreme flash sale, the pool for a hot item can be temporarily exhausted.
sentences.zh: 在极端闪购期间，热门商品的池可能会暂时耗尽。

sentences.en: When that happens, the reserve path triggers replenishment inline.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，储备路径会触发内联补货。

sentences.en: A lock ensures only one transaction replenishes at a time; other concurrent reserves for the same item wait for it to finish rather than all racing to insert rows, avoiding a thundering herd.
sentences.zh: 锁确保一次只能补充一个事务；同一项目的其他并发保留等待它完成，而不是全部竞相插入行，从而避免惊群。

sentences.en: Once replenishment completes, the waiting transactions proceed with a full pool.
sentences.zh: 补货完成后，等待交易将在满池中继续进行。

sentences.en: The buyer never sees the item as unavailable (unless it truly is).
sentences.zh: 买家永远不会认为该商品缺货（除非确实缺货）。

sentences.en: This adds latency to that specific reservation, but it preserves correctness: a buyer with available inventory is never turned away.
sentences.zh: 这会增加特定预订的延迟，但它保留了正确性：拥有可用库存的买家永远不会被拒绝。

blocks.html_en: Key technical decisions

sentences.en: Key technical decisions
sentences.zh: 关键技术决策

blocks.html_en: 1. Composite primary key: fewer locks per row

sentences.en: Composite primary key: fewer locks per row
sentences.zh: 复合主键：每行锁更少

blocks.html_en: Our first prototype used an auto-increment ID as the primary key. When we observed lock behavior (e.g. with SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS), we saw two row locks per reservation instead of one.

sentences.en: Our first prototype used an auto-increment ID as the primary key.
sentences.zh: 我们的第一个原型使用自动增量 ID 作为主键。

sentences.en: When we observed lock behavior (e.g. with SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS), we saw two row locks per reservation instead of one.
sentences.zh: 当我们观察锁行为时（例如使用 SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS），我们看到每个保留有两个行锁，而不是一个。

blocks.html_en: With an auto-increment primary key, InnoDB was locking both the secondary index used in the WHERE clause and the clustered index (primary key). We switched to a composite primary key (shop_id, inventory_item_id, inventory_group_id, id) so the columns we filter on are part of the primary key. That reduced to one lock per row, which was important when running many reservations per second.

sentences.en: With an auto-increment primary key, InnoDB was locking both the secondary index used in the WHERE clause and the clustered index (primary key).
sentences.zh: 使用自动增量主键，InnoDB 锁定 WHERE 子句中使用的辅助索引和聚集索引（主键）。

sentences.en: We switched to a composite primary key (shop_id, inventory_item_id, inventory_group_id, id) so the columns we filter on are part of the primary key.
sentences.zh: 我们切换到复合主键（shop_id、inventory_item_id、inventory_group_id、id），因此我们筛选的列是主键的一部分。

sentences.en: That reduced to one lock per row, which was important when running many reservations per second.
sentences.zh: 这减少到每行一个锁，这在每秒运行许多预留时非常重要。

blocks.html_en: Takeaway: at this scale, index and primary key design directly affect lock count and throughput.

sentences.en: Takeaway: at this scale, index and primary key design directly affect lock count and throughput.
sentences.zh: 要点：在这种规模下，索引和主键设计直接影响锁计数和吞吐量。

blocks.html_en: 2. READ COMMITTED: avoiding gap (supremum) locks

sentences.en: READ COMMITTED: avoiding gap (supremum) locks
sentences.zh: READ COMMITTED：避免间隙（最高）锁

blocks.html_en: When we ran SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on an empty table that needed replenishment, we saw gap locks (including on the "supremum" pseudo-record). Those locks blocked the replenishment transaction from inserting new rows and could lead to deadlocks.

sentences.en: When we ran SELECT ...
sentences.zh: 当我们运行 SELECT ...

sentences.en: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on an empty table that needed replenishment, we saw gap locks (including on the "supremum" pseudo-record).
sentences.zh: 对于需要补充的空表上的 UPDATE SKIP LOCKED，我们看到了间隙锁（包括“最高”伪记录上的锁）。

sentences.en: Those locks blocked the replenishment transaction from inserting new rows and could lead to deadlocks.
sentences.zh: 这些锁阻止补充事务插入新行，并可能导致死锁。

blocks.html_en: We changed the transaction isolation level from REPEATABLE READ (MySQL default) to READ COMMITTED for these transactions. Under READ COMMITTED, InnoDB doesn't take gap locks in the same way, so replenishment could proceed. Jahfer Husain's guide to InnoDB locking was very helpful for understanding this. This was our first use of a non-default isolation level in this codebase; it required small framework support for setting isolation per transaction.

sentences.en: We changed the transaction isolation level from REPEATABLE READ (MySQL default) to READ COMMITTED for these transactions.
sentences.zh: 我们将这些事务的事务隔离级别从 REPEATABLE READ（MySQL 默认）更改为 READ COMMITTED。

sentences.en: Under READ COMMITTED, InnoDB doesn't take gap locks in the same way, so replenishment could proceed.
sentences.zh: 在 READ COMMITTED 下，InnoDB 不会以相同的方式获取间隙锁，因此可以继续进行补充。

sentences.en: Jahfer Husain's guide to InnoDB locking was very helpful for understanding this.
sentences.zh: Jahfer Husain 的 InnoDB 锁定指南对于理解这一点非常有帮助。

sentences.en: This was our first use of a non-default isolation level in this codebase; it required small framework support for setting isolation per transaction.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在此代码库中第一次使用非默认隔离级别；它需要小型框架支持来设置每个事务的隔离。

blocks.html_en: 3. Consistent lock ordering: avoiding deadlocks

sentences.en: Consistent lock ordering: avoiding deadlocks
sentences.zh: 一致的锁顺序：避免死锁

blocks.html_en: We hit deadlocks when reserve and claim touched two tables in different orders. Reserve was doing INSERT into reserved_quantities then DELETE from reservation_units; claim was doing DELETE from reserved_quantities. Different transactions could lock the two tables in different orders and form a cycle.

sentences.en: We hit deadlocks when reserve and claim touched two tables in different orders.
sentences.zh: 当储备和索赔以不同的顺序触及两个表时，我们陷入了僵局。

sentences.en: Reserve was doing INSERT into reserved_quantities then DELETE from reservation_units; claim was doing DELETE from reserved_quantities.
sentences.zh: Reserve正在对reserved_quantities进行INSERT，然后从reservation_units进行DELETE；声明正在从保留数量中进行删除。

sentences.en: Different transactions could lock the two tables in different orders and form a cycle.
sentences.zh: 不同的事务可以以不同的顺序锁定两个表，形成一个循环。

blocks.html_en: The fix was to standardize the order: reserve always DELETEs from the units table first, then INSERTs into reserved_quantities. Claim only touches reserved_quantities. Because both paths now acquire locks in the same order, neither can hold a lock the other is waiting for—no more circular waits.

sentences.en: The fix was to standardize the order: reserve always DELETEs from the units table first, then INSERTs into reserved_quantities.
sentences.zh: 解决方法是标准化顺序：保留总是首先从单位表中删除，然后插入到保留数量中。

sentences.en: Claim only touches reserved_quantities.
sentences.zh: 声明仅涉及保留数量。

sentences.en: Because both paths now acquire locks in the same order, neither can hold a lock the other is waiting for—no more circular waits.
sentences.zh: 因为两条路径现在都以相同的顺序获取锁，所以两者都无法持有对方正在等待的锁，不再有循环等待。

sentences.en: Batching with UNION ALL
sentences.zh: 使用 UNION ALL 进行批处理

sentences.en: Each round trip to the database has a cost.
sentences.zh: 数据库的每次往返都有成本。

sentences.en: For carts with multiple line items, we batch reservation queries using UNION ALL so we fetch all needed units in one round trip:
sentences.zh: 对于具有多个订单项的购物车，我们使用 UNION ALL 批量预订查询，以便在一次往返中获取所有需要的单位：

blocks.html_en: That cut total round trips and helped latency under load.

sentences.en: That cut total round trips and helped latency under load.
sentences.zh: 这减少了总往返次数并减少了负载下的延迟。

blocks.html_en: The real bottleneck: connections, not CPU

sentences.en: The real bottleneck: connections, not CPU
sentences.zh: 真正的瓶颈：连接，而不是CPU

blocks.html_en: In production we hit a throughput ceiling well below our target. Reservation latency (e.g. P90) was acceptable, CPU wasn't maxed out, and the queries were already optimized. So we looked elsewhere.

sentences.en: In production we hit a throughput ceiling well below our target.
sentences.zh: 在生产中，我们的吞吐量上限远低于我们的目标。

sentences.en: Reservation latency (e.g. P90) was acceptable, CPU wasn't maxed out, and the queries were already optimized.
sentences.zh: 预留延迟（例如 P90）是可以接受的，CPU 没有达到最大，并且查询已经优化。

sentences.en: So we looked elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把目光转向别处。

blocks.html_en: We tried batching reservations across multiple checkouts in a single SKIP LOCKED query to use fewer connections. That helped in load tests but added complexity. We also moved some read load to replicas. Still, something didn't add up.

sentences.en: We tried batching reservations across multiple checkouts in a single SKIP LOCKED query to use fewer connections.
sentences.zh: 我们尝试在单个 SKIP LOCKED 查询中跨多个结账进行批量预订，以使用更少的连接。

sentences.en: That helped in load tests but added complexity.
sentences.zh: 这有助于负载测试，但增加了复杂性。

sentences.en: We also moved some read load to replicas.
sentences.zh: 我们还将一些读取负载移至副本。

sentences.en: Still, something didn't add up.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，还是有些事情没有加起来。

sentences.en: Following the symptoms

blocks.html_en: During load tests we saw:

sentences.en: During load tests we saw:

blocks.html_en: • Threads queuing in MySQL

sentences.en: Threads queuing in MySQL
sentences.zh: MySQL 中的线程排队

blocks.html_en: • Connection exhaustion to MySQL backends on ProxySQL layer

sentences.en: Connection exhaustion to MySQL backends on ProxySQL layer
sentences.zh: ProxySQL 层上 MySQL 后端的连接耗尽

blocks.html_en: So we added visibility into which business processes were holding database connections and for how long. Knowing that connections are exhausted doesn't tell you who is holding them. We needed per-caller attribution.

sentences.en: So we added visibility into which business processes were holding database connections and for how long.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们增加了对哪些业务流程持有数据库连接以及持续时间的可见性。

sentences.en: Knowing that connections are exhausted doesn't tell you who is holding them.
sentences.zh: 知道连接已耗尽并不能告诉您谁在持有它们。

sentences.en: We needed per-caller attribution.
sentences.zh: 我们需要每个呼叫者的归因。

blocks.html_en: On the application side, we annotated every SQL statement with a comment tag identifying the business process, like /* conn_tag:checkout_completion */. On the ProxySQL layer, we added tracking that parses the tag and measures how long each caller holds a connection. The result: total connection hold time, broken down by business process.

sentences.en: On the application side, we annotated every SQL statement with a comment tag identifying the business process, like /* conn_tag:checkout_completion */.
sentences.zh: 在应用程序方面，我们使用标识业务流程的注释标记来注释每个 SQL 语句，例如 /* conn_tag:checkout_completion */。

sentences.en: On the ProxySQL layer, we added tracking that parses the tag and measures how long each caller holds a connection.
sentences.zh: 在 ProxySQL 层上，我们添加了跟踪来解析标签并测量每个调用者保持连接的时间。

sentences.en: The result: total connection hold time, broken down by business process.
sentences.zh: 结果：总连接保持时间，按业务流程细分。

blocks.html_en: This immediately showed which callers were consuming the most connection time. Not which queries were slow, but which processes were holding connections across long transactions. If you're hitting connection limits and can't tell why, this pattern (tag at the app layer, aggregate at the proxy) is straightforward to implement and immediately actionable.

sentences.en: This immediately showed which callers were consuming the most connection time.
sentences.zh: 这立即显示了哪些呼叫者消耗了最多的连接时间。

sentences.en: Not which queries were slow, but which processes were holding connections across long transactions.
sentences.zh: 不是哪些查询速度慢，而是哪些进程在长事务中保持连接。

sentences.en: If you're hitting connection limits and can't tell why, this pattern (tag at the app layer, aggregate at the proxy) is straightforward to implement and immediately actionable.
sentences.zh: 如果您遇到连接限制并且无法判断原因，则此模式（应用程序层的标记，代理处的聚合）很容易实现并且可以立即采取行动。

blocks.html_en: What we found

sentences.en: What we found
sentences.zh: 我们发现了什么

blocks.html_en: Once we could see connection usage, we learned that reservations weren't the only heavy user. Other parts of the checkout path were holding connections longer than necessary. They hadn't been optimized because they hadn't been the first to hit the limit. Connections are finite: at high throughput we need many short transactions per second. When other code held connections longer, reservations were the straw that broke the camel's back—not because reservations were slow, but because the pool was already near depletion.

content_html_zh:
在结账过程中，当买家点击“完成购买”时，我们需要保证他们购买的商品仍然可用。 如果我们在一个方向上犯了这个错误，两个买家会购买相同的最后一件商品：商家必须取消订单，发送一封道歉电子邮件，并承担支持成本。 如果我们在另一个方向上搞错了，我们会告诉买家某样东西已经售罄，而实际上并没有，而商家则失去了他们本应完成的销售。

在 Shopify 的规模下，任何一种失败都会迅速加剧。 2025 年黑色星期五，我们平台上的商家每分钟销售额达到创纪录的 510 万美元。 这些交易中的每一笔都涉及库存。

我们的超售保护系统通过在付款处理期间保留库存来解决这个问题，这是一种短期保留，可以防止两个并发结账认领同一单位。 多年来，它一直在 Redis 上运行。 当我们转向统一数据库策略时，我们必须回答一个难题：MySQL 能否处理相同的规模？

早期的尝试都失败了。 具有数量列的单行无法处理争用。 MySQL 8 的 SKIP LOCKED 功能引入了不同的设计：每个库存单元一行，而不是每个项目一行。 受到 37signals 数据库支持的负载分配方法的启发，我们重建了 MySQL 预留，并在 2025 年流量高峰期间达到了高吞吐量目标。

但最难的一课并不是数据库设计。 它发现真正的瓶颈并不是我们所观察和测量的。 这篇文章将介绍该解决方案以及我们在此过程中发现的内容。

挑战

什么是超卖保护？

超卖保护主要有两个操作：

  • 保留：当付款开始时，我们将项目标记为保留（短暂保留，例如几分钟）。
  • 索赔：付款成功后，我们会从库存分类帐中永久扣除数量（事实来源）。

结帐的完成取决于其速度和正确性。 缓慢的预订会引发限制和更糟糕的买家体验。 错误意味着过度销售（愤怒的客户）或销售不足（收入损失）。

规模和正确性要求

这里的规模并不是抽象的：Shopify 占据了超过 14% 的美国电子商务市场，在 2025 年黑色星期五，我们看到每分钟的销售额比去年同期增长了 11%。 每次涉及库存的结账都会进行预订，因此系统必须在不丢弃请求或破坏一致性的情况下处理突发情况。

我们需要：

  • 在高峰流量期间支持平台的高性能吞吐量目标
  • 尊重多地点库存（仅从可以履行的地点进行预订）
  • 在预订和库存分类账之间保持 ACID 保证
  • 优先考虑正确性：不超售，不丢失预订

Redis 模型及其局限性

以前的系统将预订存储在 Redis 中。 每个项目都有一个数量键，保留意味着 DECR，释放意味着 INCR。 Redis 可以很好地处理并发性，但预订和库存分类账位于两个不同的系统中。

索赔步骤（处理付款、永久扣除库存）需要更新 MySQL 和清理 Redis，而这两个操作无法包含在单个原子步骤中。 根据订单，这可能会导致超售（商品已售出但从未从分类账中扣除）或卖空（商品已扣除但仍标记为保留）。

最重要的是，Redis 模型没有多位置意识，并且增加了维护单独集群的运营成本。 将预订转移到与账本相同的 MySQL 数据库中意味着我们可以将所有内容包装在 ACID 事务中，并完全消除这些故障模式。

解决方案：跳过锁定

核心理念：每单元一行，以设计为界

我们使用每个可销售单位一行，而不是每个商品一行包含数量列。 包含 10 个单位的项目有 10 行。 保留三个单元意味着在单个事务中选择并移动三行。 通过将预订和库存分类账保存在同一个数据库中，我们可以在预订和索赔之间获得 ACID - 修复 Redis 可能出现的错误类别（例如，付款成功但库存未索赔，反之亦然）。

简化的储备流程如下所示：

SKIP LOCKED 使其具有可扩展性：如果另一个事务锁定了某些行，MySQL 会跳过它们并返回其他可用行。 无需在同一排等待，减少争用。

但是，所有库存的每单位一行将出现大规模故障 - 跨 10 个位置的 50,000 单位的商品意味着 500,000 行，并且储备查询在扫描它们时会变慢。 相反，我们维护一个有界的可用行池，每个项目/位置组合的上限为 1,000。 预留消耗该池中的行；补货流程会从库存分类账中重新填充它。

为什么是 1,000？ 上限需要足够大，以吸收突发而不至于耗尽，但又足够小，以保持表紧凑和 SKIP LOCKED 扫描快速。 我们根据在闪购期间观察到的每个商品/位置的峰值预订率来确定其大小：1,000 为我们提供了足够的空间，可以在持续负载下保持补货，而不会导致表增长到查询性能下降的程度。

如果池空了会发生什么？ 在极端闪购期间，热门商品的池可能会暂时耗尽。 当这种情况发生时，储备路径会触发内联补货。 锁确保一次只能补充一个事务；同一项目的其他并发保留等待它完成，而不是全部竞相插入行，从而避免惊群。 补货完成后，等待交易将在满池中继续进行。 买家永远不会认为该商品缺货（除非确实缺货）。 这会增加特定预订的延迟，但它保留了正确性：拥有可用库存的买家永远不会被拒绝。

关键技术决策

1. 复合主键：每行锁更少

我们的第一个原型使用自动增量 ID 作为主键。 当我们观察锁行为时（例如使用 SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS），我们看到每个保留有两个行锁，而不是一个。

使用自动增量主键，InnoDB 锁定 WHERE 子句中使用的辅助索引和聚集索引（主键）。 我们切换到复合主键（shop_id、inventory_item_id、inventory_group_id、id），因此我们筛选的列是主键的一部分。 这减少到每行一个锁，这在每秒运行许多预留时非常重要。

要点：在这种规模下，索引和主键设计直接影响锁计数和吞吐量。

2. READ COMMITTED：避免间隙（最高）锁

当我们运行 SELECT ... 对于需要补充的空表上的 UPDATE SKIP LOCKED，我们看到了间隙锁（包括“最高”伪记录上的锁）。 这些锁阻止补充事务插入新行，并可能导致死锁。

我们将这些事务的事务隔离级别从 REPEATABLE READ（MySQL 默认）更改为 READ COMMITTED。 在 READ COMMITTED 下，InnoDB 不会以相同的方式获取间隙锁，因此可以继续进行补充。 Jahfer Husain 的 InnoDB 锁定指南对于理解这一点非常有帮助。 这是我们在此代码库中第一次使用非默认隔离级别；它需要小型框架支持来设置每个事务的隔离。

3. 一致的锁顺序：避免死锁

当储备和索赔以不同的顺序触及两个表时，我们陷入了僵局。 Reserve正在对reserved_quantities进行INSERT，然后从reservation_units进行DELETE；声明正在从保留数量中进行删除。 不同的事务可以以不同的顺序锁定两个表，形成一个循环。

解决方法是标准化顺序：保留总是首先从单位表中删除，然后插入到保留数量中。 声明仅涉及保留数量。 因为两条路径现在都以相同的顺序获取锁，所以两者都无法持有对方正在等待的锁，不再有循环等待。

4. 使用 UNION ALL 进行批处理

数据库的每次往返都有成本。 对于具有多个订单项的购物车，我们使用 UNION ALL 批量预订查询，以便在一次往返中获取所有需要的单位：

这减少了总往返次数并减少了负载下的延迟。

真正的瓶颈：连接，而不是CPU

在生产中，我们的吞吐量上限远低于我们的目标。 预留延迟（例如 P90）是可以接受的，CPU 没有达到最大，并且查询已经优化。 所以我们把目光转向别处。

我们尝试在单个 SKIP LOCKED 查询中跨多个结账进行批量预订，以使用更少的连接。 这有助于负载测试，但增加了复杂性。 我们还将一些读取负载移至副本。 尽管如此，还是有些事情没有加起来。

出现症状后

在负载测试期间我们看到：

  • MySQL 中的线程排队
  • 排队工作运行时 CPU 出现峰值
  • ProxySQL 层上 MySQL 后端的连接耗尽

因此，我们增加了对哪些业务流程持有数据库连接以及持续时间的可见性。 知道连接已耗尽并不能告诉您谁在持有它们。 我们需要每个呼叫者的归因。

在应用程序方面，我们使用标识业务流程的注释标记来注释每个 SQL 语句，例如 /* conn_tag:checkout_completion */。 在 ProxySQL 层上，我们添加了跟踪来解析标签并测量每个调用者保持连接的时间。 结果：总连接保持时间，按业务流程细分。

这立即显示了哪些呼叫者消耗了最多的连接时间。 不是哪些查询速度慢，而是哪些进程在长事务中保持连接。 如果您遇到连接限制并且无法判断原因，则此模式（应用程序层的标记，代理处的聚合）很容易实现并且可以立即采取行动。

我们发现了什么

一旦我们看到连接使用情况，我们就了解到预订并不是唯一的重度用户。 结账路径的其他部分保持连接的时间超过了必要的时间。 它们没有被优化，因为它们不是第一个达到极限的。 连接是有限的：在高吞吐量下，我们每秒需要许多短事务。 当其他代码保持连接的时间更长时，预留就是压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草——不是因为预留很慢，而是因为池已经接近耗尽。

结帐路径的清理删除了主数据库上 50% 的读取和 33% 的事务。 我们还重新审视了 MySQL 配置。 InnoDB 线程并发数早在几年前就已被保守地设置，并且从未重新评估过。 我们的工作量发生了变化。 在我们有空间的情况下增加线程并发性后，我们消除了直到我们并排连接和 CPU 指标时才发现的瓶颈。

结合起来，清理和配置更改消除了上限。 我们可以超越之前的限制并实现我们的目标。 在大批量闪存销售期间，写入器 CPU 保持在 50% 以下，读取器 CPU 保持在 16% 以下，还有剩余空间。

切换

我们没有从 Redis 切换到 MySQL。 我们以所谓的“影子模式”并行运行两个系统：每个保留都写入 Redis 和 MySQL，而 Redis 仍然是事实来源。 这让我们可以并排比较两个系统，验证 MySQL 产生了正确的业务成果并满足我们对实际生产流量的性能要求。 由于这两个系统均已上线，因此无需迁移飞行中的预订。 当 MySQL 建立自己的状态时，Redis 保留继续得到尊重。

一旦我们对正确性和性能感到满意，我们就将事实来源切换到 MySQL。 如果出现任何问题，我们可以通过终止开关恢复到 Redis；双写入路径仍然处于活动状态，因此 Redis 始终可以完整地查看预订情况。 推出是循序渐进的，从低流量的 Pod 开始，一直到流量最大的商家。

我们学到了什么

我们从这个项目中学到了很多东西，但有两个主要收获：

1. 重新审视旧的决定

五年前不可能实现的事情（例如，使用 MySQL 来完成此工作负载）现在可以通过 SKIP LOCKED 等新功能实现。 配置也是如此：当工作负载和硬件发展时，线程限制和其他“经验法则”设置值得重新检查。 如果数字加起来不合理（例如，CPU 较低但需要排队），请深入研究。

2. 从小事做起并观察

我们从最小的原型中获得了很多价值：一个小的 ruby​​ 脚本和 MySQL，没有像 Rails 这样的完整框架。 观察数据库（例如第二个终端中的锁定行为）教会我们的不仅仅是理论。 在探索时，简单的工具和严格的反馈循环击败了大型、不透明的系统。

MySQL 现在可以处理我们过去假设所需的专用基础设施的工作负载。 如果您要使用 Redis、Kafka 或自定义协调层来实现高吞吐量互斥，那么您现有的数据库可能已经足够了。

瓶颈不在我们预期的地方。 我们优化查询和锁定数周；真正的限制是我们甚至没有查看的代码中的连接使用情况。 如果数字加起来不合理（CPU 较低但排队较多），请检测完整路径。 答案通常在于管道，而不是发动机。

至关重要的是，这并不是为了快速预订。 这是为了让他们成为安全的邻居。 预订与购物车更新、付款处理和订单创建共享数据库。 连接饱和或持有锁时间过长的系统会危及所有这些连接。 真正的障碍是维持吞吐量而不降低数据库的其他一切健康状况。

对我们来说，回报是具体的：更可靠的预订意味着不会出现超额销售，并且可以从我们的商家处获得更成功的购买。
